historicalReferences: Alain Prost clinched the 1987 title here after a dramatic race, a moment etched in the memory of every Brazilian motorsport fan.
Who can forget Nigel Mansell's dominant win in 1989, showcasing his raw speed and determination on this very layout?
The 1981 race saw Carlos Reutemann take victory, a bittersweet moment for the home crowd as Nelson Piquet struggled with reliability.
This track has seen its fair share of drama. In 1988, Thierry Boutsen secured his first podium finish in torrential conditions.
The Brazilian Grand Prix here has often been a race of attrition, with the demanding circuit and unpredictable weather taking their toll.
Ayrton Senna's early battles at Jacarepaguá helped cement his reputation as a future star, showcasing his incredible car control on this fast circuit.
The 1986 race was a classic, with Nelson Piquet holding off Ayrton Senna in a nail-biting finish that had the crowd on its feet.
Michael Schumacher's victories here in the late 90s and early 2000s demonstrated his mastery of this circuit, showcasing his strategic brilliance.
The 2005 layout was specifically designed to improve safety, after some very close calls in previous years on the longer original circuit. While faster, it still demands precision.
This circuit hosted the Formula One Grand Prix from 1978 to 1990, witnessing some legendary performances and championship-deciding moments.

The high-speed nature of this circuit puts a lot of stress on the tires. Managing tire temperatures will be crucial for maintaining performance.
